class_binding_note: The card's class_id is GLOBAL, but the reviewed instrument is class-bound: its frozen_classes block (lines 52-118) is the class-id authority for every claim the audit admits. I therefore bound the class-facing checks to the four frozen ids and re-measured them against research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml (sha256 0abb9ed8a961, the G-F0-passed rev5).
hard_failures: HF-05-adjacent (critical; the A0 taxonomy has no code for 'gate artifact whose declared self-test is unrecorded'): acceptance cannot bind at this hash because the artifact's own precondition fails. The validation block (lines 45-50) declares validator artifacts/audit/audit_run.py (exists, sha256 3b27dd3fef7f) but leaves last_run: null, last_run_result: null and report_sha256: null, while line 46 states 'a rubric with no passing self-test is not a gate'. No passing self-test of the reviewed bytes is recorded in the artifact. reviews/INDEX.md:37 asserts 'A0 rubric materialized and self-tested', but that INDEX (sha256 73b7b92a9b) was generated 2026-09-11T23:27:56+08:00, before the reviewed bytes (mtime 23:28), and the artifact itself records no such run, so the assertion is unsupported at d748a9e3574e.

HF-06-adjacent (critical; no exact code for 'acceptance test not bound to named evidence'): the acceptance item 'every acceptance test machine-checkable or reviewer-adjudicated with named evidence' fails. Only verifiers.schema_formulation (line 23) carries an evidence field; verifiers.literature (line 31), verifiers.numerics (line 37) and verifiers.formalization (line 43) each carry a human_adjudication_only item with no evidence object, and none of the 28 checks[] entries across the four blocks names a detector (contrast hard_failures, where all 14 entries carry a detector). A reviewer of those three task types cannot bind accept/reject to a named evidence object at this hash; even the schema evidence string names 'one linter verdict' without a path.

HF-14-adjacent (major): the HF-14 detector's field vocabulary does not match the live ledger schema it must run on. HF-14 (lines 243-252) detects 'status=accepted / validation_status=passed / supports_claim=true with no independent reviewer verdict'. On the live ledger (ledger/theorems.jsonl sha256 a1674f094979, 62 records) the literal strings 'status=accepted' and 'supports_claim=true' occur 0 times; T-201..T-203 carry author_asserts_supports: true, review_status: not_independently_reviewed and acceptance_authority 'astra-lead-literature (ledger author; author self-assessment, not a reviewer verdict)'. The self-certification pattern HF-14 exists to catch is still live, but a literal implementation of the detector has zero recall on the current bytes.

findings.finding: The two dated evidence anchors do not meet the evidence rule the audit enforces elsewhere (PROTOCOL.md rule 4: cite as path#sha256-prefix or path:line). HF-13 cites 'astra-lead-literature.log line 10', which does not resolve at the repo root; the file is at runtime/logs/astra-lead-literature.log (sha256 5d5b72690d17). HF-13's artifacts/worker-06/class_binding_rules.json (line 240) exists (sha256 a30606136747) but is cited path-only, and HF-14's 'ledger/theorems.jsonl entries T-201..T-203' (line 251) is cited path-only. No HF anchor carries a #sha256.
findings.remedy: Repoint the log reference to runtime/logs/astra-lead-literature.log:10 and append #sha256 prefixes to both artifact anchors.

findings.finding: novel_accepted_coverage is the only one of the 7 metrics with no target key; the other six declare one (class_binding 1.0, citation_support 1.0, hard_failure_rate <= 0.10, duplication <= 0.25, effective_sample_size 'report ESS, never nominal n', information_gain '> 0 net of null control'). A consumer of the rubric cannot tell pass from fail for this metric.
findings.remedy: Add an explicit target, e.g. '>= 1/4 per gate window', matching the metric's definition.

findings.finding: The definition embeds the quantitative prior 'nine independent LLM judges give ESS ~2.2' with no locator and no quantity_check, while the rubric's own G-LIT criterion (line 142) requires a quantity_check for quantitative claims and HF-04 (lines 186-190) fires on a quantity whose evidence refs lack one. HF-04's detector is claim-scoped, so it does not formally fire on a rubric field, but the audit instrument does not meet the evidence standard it imposes on the objects it audits.
findings.remedy: Cite the measurement (base HANDOFF.md section 2 or its primary record) with a hash and label ~2.2 explicitly as a project prior rather than a measured constant.

findings.finding: The 14-code HF taxonomy covers claim and artifact defects but has no code for gate-instrument defects: an unfilled validation/self-test block, an acceptance test with no detector or named evidence, and a detector whose field vocabulary is stale against the live schema. Two of the three hard failures above could only be labelled by analogy (HF-05/HF-06-adjacent), which is exactly the ambiguity the taxonomy exists to remove; a machine census of this review's own hard_failures list cannot map them to codes.
findings.remedy: Add codes such as HF-15 (gate self-test unrecorded), HF-16 (acceptance test unbound to detector or named evidence), and a schema-version clause for evidence-carrying detectors, or state explicitly that HF-01..14 are claim-scoped only.

findings.finding: The reviewer-agreement criterion ('kappa >= 0.60 on a >= 20% blind sample, or the review is re-run with a third reviewer') names no report artifact, no sampling frame and no trigger for the third-reviewer branch. Two readers would disagree on when this criterion passes, which is the disagreement test the review protocol itself applies.
findings.remedy: Name the kappa report path and the sample frame, and state the numeric trigger at which the third-reviewer branch activates.
